legalSettingsIntro.message: Every artifact Legal Capture can produce is optional. Turn off anything you don't want collected — the capture still runs and still produces a hash-sealed package with whatever is left on.

legalOptNetworkNote.message: Records the full HTTP request/response exchange for the page (headers, bodies, redirect chain, TLS details) into a standard WARC/WACZ archive, playable independently at replayweb.page. This is the core evidence that the page's content came from the real server, not a locally edited copy — turning it off removes capture.wacz, TLS details, and the redirect chain from the package entirely.

legalOptWebSocketNote.message: Records WebSocket handshakes and every frame sent or received, as a transcript inside the WARC. Relevant for sites (chat, live feeds) where the visible content arrives over a WebSocket rather than a plain HTTP response — without this, that content is on screen but has no corresponding entry in the archive.

legalOptServiceWorkerNote.message: Best-effort attach to the page's Service Worker (if any) to capture requests it intercepts or serves from its own cache — traffic a normal tab-scoped recording can't see. Matters for PWA-style sites that render content without a visible network round trip.

legalOptScreenshotNote.message: The visual capture itself (screenshot.png) — the human-readable "what did the page look like" evidence most people expect from this tool. Turning this off still produces a package, but with no image in it.

legalOptDomNote.message: Serializes the live, post-JavaScript-execution page markup (document.documentElement.outerHTML) at the same instant as the screenshot. Machine-readable evidence independent of both the raster screenshot and the raw HTTP bodies in the WARC — ties what was visually shown to the actual markup that produced it.

legalOptMhtmlNote.message: A complete, self-contained snapshot of the rendered page — markup, stylesheets, scripts, images, and fonts bundled into one file, built by Chrome itself (Page.captureSnapshot), not this extension's own code. Opens directly in Chrome/Edge or any MHTML-capable tool, independent of Sharpshooter — the strongest "the whole page, everything" artifact in the package.

legalOptTimestampsNote.message: Sends manifest.json's SHA-256 hash (never the page content itself) to independent public timestamping authorities, who sign back proof that hash existed at that moment. This is what lets you prove the capture wasn't put together after the fact — without it, the package is still hash-sealed, but the only clock backing the capture time is this computer's own.

legalOptTsaProvidersNote.message: Each additional independent authority you enable adds a separate, cross-checkable witness to the capture time — useful if one authority's availability or trustworthiness is ever questioned. Any one succeeding is enough to timestamp the capture; more is simply stronger. These only apply while the timestamps toggle above is on.

legalOptSha256SumsNote.message: A plain-text list of the SHA-256 of every file physically inside the zip, so anyone can do a five-second check that nothing was swapped after the package was assembled. Not the core integrity mechanism — manifest.json's own sealed hash (always computed) is — this is just a convenience on top.

legalOperatorFieldsNote.message: Free-text, optional, printed on report.txt and recorded (unverified) in manifest.json — always included when filled in, not gated by a toggle.

legalOptPageEnvNote.message: Records the captured tab's screen size, pixel ratio, color depth, locale, IANA timezone name, hardware thread count, and basic document metadata (title, referrer). Documents the rendering context the screenshot was taken under — no special browser permission required.

legalOptMachineNote.message: Records the operator's own computer's CPU model/core count, installed RAM, and connected display layout/resolution — a hardware fingerprint of the device that produced the capture, for chain-of-custody purposes. Requires a one-time browser permission grant the first time you turn this on. Off by default since it's new information about your own machine, not the captured page.

legalOptGeolocationNote.message: Records the operator's physical location (via the browser's Geolocation API — GPS, Wi-Fi, or IP-based, whichever the OS provides) at the moment of capture. Can support a chain-of-custody claim of where the capture was performed. Requires a one-time browser permission grant, and the browser will prompt for location access on first use. Off by default — this is sensitive personal data about you, the operator, not the page you're capturing.

legalOptAccountEmailNote.message: Records the email of the Google account currently signed into this Chrome profile, if any — a stronger operator-identity signal than the free-text Operator Name field on the main view, since it comes from account ownership rather than a typed string. Requires a one-time browser permission grant. Off by default, since your Chrome account may not be the identity you want tied to a specific capture.

legalSettingsAbout.message: Legal Capture is built to let a screenshot be presented as evidence with a case for its own authenticity, not just an image someone could have edited. With everything above left on, one click: (1) starts recording the page's real network traffic, (2) forces a fresh, cache-bypassed reload — so any prior manual DOM edit (e.g. Remove Elements) or live DevTools tampering is undone before anything is captured, (3) takes the screenshot plus independent DOM and full-page MHTML snapshots of the exact same moment, (4) bundles the recorded network traffic into a standard WARC/WACZ archive anyone can replay independently of this extension, (5) builds a manifest listing the SHA-256 hash of every file in the package and freezes it, (6) sends only that manifest's hash — never the page content — to independent public timestamping authorities (RFC 3161), who sign back cryptographic proof the hash existed at that moment, and (7) zips everything, including a plain-language report explaining exactly what was and wasn't captured, into one file you save yourself. Every step above is individually optional; manifest.json always records exactly which options were on for a given capture, so the package itself is the audit trail of what it does and doesn't contain. This tool produces supporting technical evidence, not a legal determination — consult counsel on how to present it.

reencodeNote.message: Flattens captures onto a white background and strips the alpha channel and colour-profile chunks. Fixes Adobe ScriptUI / Direct2D drawbot panels that reject the screenshots (HRESULT 0x80070057).

filenamePrefixNote.message: Prepended to every saved file: prefix-domain-timestamp.png

defaultQualityNote.message: Used when a preset is set to "Default". Per-preset overrides take precedence.

presetsNote.message: Shown as buttons on the main view. The Custom preset is always kept. Smart presets (User, Full Page, Vertical) auto-derive their dimensions from the active tab.

defaultCropNote.message: Every capture goes straight to the crop editor. The separate "with crop" buttons are hidden while this is on.

fullPageCapNote.message: Caps the Full Page preset height. Hard maximum is 16384 px (Chrome's limit).

navTooltipNote.message: Shows a small tip next to the highlight frame in Capture Element and Remove Elements, explaining how to walk the DOM with the scroll wheel, arrow keys and mouse (↑↓ for depth, ←→ for siblings).

legalCaptureEnabledNote.message: Adds a specialist capture mode that produces a forensic evidence package (WACZ archive + independent RFC 3161 timestamp) for legal / investigative use. Off by default to keep the main popup simple.

helpDisclaimer.message: Heads up: websites change their page structure over time. If a capture looks wrong, try Page Capture or a different target element with Capture Element.

helpPageCapture.message:
Page Capture

Captures the whole page at a chosen resolution. Pick a preset:

  • User — the current tab's viewport size (default). Combined with the 2× quality multiplier, gives you a sharp shot at the exact size you see in the browser.
  • Full Page — viewport width, full document height (measured live).
  • Vertical — viewport width × (width × 3.5), good for long, tall pages.
  • FullHD — 1920 × 1080.
  • 4K — 3840 × 2160.
  • Custom — your own width × height.

The page is emulated at this resolution before capture, so layouts adapt as if the window were that size.

helpCaptureElement.message:
Capture Element

Click the button, then hover any element on the page. A cyan glow shows what will be captured. Use the scroll wheel or ↑ / ↓ to change depth (up = parent, down = first child) and ← / → to step to the previous / next sibling. Click or press Enter to commit.

helpQuality.message:
Quality multiplier

1× / 2× / 3× / 4× — scales pixel density. 2× is the default and works well for most uses. 3×–4× produces large but very sharp images suitable for print or motion graphics.

helpHelpers.message:
Helpers

Remove Elements — manual click-to-remove mode. Hover targets, use the wheel or ↑ / ↓ to change depth and ← / → to step between siblings, then click or press Enter to delete. Ctrl/Cmd+Z undoes the last removal; ESC stops.

helpFeedback.message:
Feedback & issues

In case of any issues with the extension or any feedback — forward to chemradio@gmail.com.

Extension was built by Timur Timaev with help of Claude.

designSettingsIntro.message: Pick what a design extraction produces. With one artifact selected you get that file on its own; with several you get a zip.

designExtractEnabledNote.message: Adds a helper that reads an element's colours, typography, spacing, radii, shadows and hover states, and produces a shareable spec card plus a Markdown sheet and JSON. Everything is read locally — no new permissions, nothing sent anywhere.

designOptCardNote.message: A shareable image: the element, its palette as real swatches, a type specimen, drawn padding and corner radius, hover changes, and any contrast failures. This is the one to paste into a chat or a deck.

designOptScreenshotNote.message: The element on its own, captured exactly as Element Capture would. Also used as the card's hero image — with this off the card still renders, without the preview.

designOptSpecNote.message: Every value as Markdown tables — palette, type scale, spacing, radii, shadows, layout, states, contrast and tokens. Pastes into a document or issue tracker with its formatting intact.

designOptJsonNote.message: The complete dossier, including per-element computed styles. This is what the card and the spec sheet are both rendered from.

designOptStatesNote.message: Forces each pseudo-class in turn and records only what changes. A button's hover style is half its spec, and it can't be read any other way. Adds a moment to the capture and briefly flickers the element.

designOptTokensNote.message: Reads the CSS variables in scope on the element. If the site is built on design tokens these are its actual system, which is worth more than the flattened values they resolve to.

designOptContrastNote.message: Grades each text colour against the surface it is actually painted on, using the 3:1 threshold for large text and 4.5:1 otherwise.

designCardThemeNote.message: Light reproduces better in decks, docs and print, so it's the default regardless of the popup's own theme.

designHowBody.message: Pick an element the same way as Element Capture — hover to highlight, wheel or arrow keys to walk the DOM, Esc to cancel. On click the extension screenshots it, then reads the computed styles of every element inside it and compares them against browser defaults, so you get the values the site's authors actually set rather than a dump of everything.

designHowLimits.message: One thing worth knowing: browsers resolve CSS before it can be read, so clamp(), percentages, em and vw all arrive as pixels measured at the capture width. Styles inside shadow DOM, iframes and canvas can't be read at all and are listed as gaps. Font files are referenced, never embedded.
